claim: RouteNote accepts some AI-generated releases but will NOT deliver AI content to Korean partner stores (Melon, Genie, Bugs, FLO, VIBE), Amazon, or Content Recognition (YouTube Content ID).
correction: Accurate as of 2026-09-06, per search-engine snippets of RouteNote's KB article (the live page is blocked from this environment, so re-check directly before publishing). RouteNote states it 'will accept some AI-generated content' but that AI-generated content cannot be delivered to its Content Recognition DSP options (which include YouTube Content ID), to the Korean partner stores Melon, Genie, Bugs, FLO and VIBE, or to Amazon. A companion article ('Why is my release blocked on Korean stores?', https://support.routenote.com/kb-article/why-is-my-release-blocked-on-korean-stores/) repeats that Korean partner stores do not accept AI-generated releases; releases made with AI aid are allowed on RouteNote but are blocked from Korean stores. Two additional conditions worth adding to the guide: (1) you must be prepared to provide links to the AI-generation sites you used, or RouteNote may be unable to approve the content, and RouteNote asks that you use services with ethical training models; (2) releases containing AI-generated or AI-assisted content 'may be subject to additional review and may take longer than the standard moderation timeframe.'
evidence_quote: AI-generated content is unable to be delivered to RouteNote's Content Recognition DSP options as well as Korean partner stores (Melon, Genie, Bugs, Flo, and Vibe) and Amazon.

claim: RouteNote release review currently takes 25-27 business days, plus 7-14 days for store ingestion.
correction: Substantially correct but time-sensitive, and only verifiable via search-engine snippets because the live page is blocked from this environment. The most recent snippet (search engine reported the page as 'updated 5 days ago' relative to 2026-09-06) reads: moderation team 'currently approving content within 25-27 working days (Monday-Friday) after submission', described as longer than usual due to a high volume of submissions. An older cached snippet of the same page read '23-25 working days ... roughly 5 weeks', so the figure changes frequently; the guide should cite it with a 'checked on' date and link readers to the article rather than hard-coding the number. RouteNote's own wording is 'working days (Monday-Friday)', not 'business days', and the estimate assumes no further action is required from the uploader. Store ingestion: after approval the distribution team sends the release to stores within 24 hours; it can take 7-14 days from the approval date to be fully ingested; Spotify and Apple Music are typically live within 5 days of approval. Directly relevant to this guide: AI-generated or AI-assisted releases may be subject to additional review and take longer than the standard timeframe, and a release sent back for changes will be delayed further.
evidence_quote: The RouteNote moderation team are currently approving content within 25-27 working days (Monday-Friday) after submission ... It can take 7-14 days from your approved date for your release to be fully ingested into your selected stores.

claim: RouteNote Free pays 85% of revenue; RouteNote Premium pays 100% and costs about $9.99 per year per single (check the current price). RouteNote audio spec: stereo FLAC or MP3, 16-bit, 44.1 kHz; flags clipping, over 8 s of leading/trailing silence.
correction: Revenue split and audio spec are accurate; the Premium price wording needs correcting. As of 2026-09-06 (via search-engine snippets of RouteNote support articles; live pages blocked from this environment): Free plan pays 85% of net revenue (RouteNote keeps 15%); Premium pays 100% (RouteNote keeps 0%) — source https://support.routenote.com/kb-article/what-percentage-does-routenote-take/. Premium pricing is a one-off first-year fee by release size, then a renewal: $10 Single (1 track), $20 EP (2-6 tracks), $30 Album (7-18 tracks), $45 Extended Album (19+ tracks), and 'after your first year, there's a $9.99 annual subscription fee if you choose to keep the release Premium' — so a single is $10 upfront, then $9.99/year, not a flat $9.99/year (source https://support.routenote.com/kb-article/how-much-does-premium-cost/). Audio spec confirmed: 'Audio must be formatted in stereo as a FLAC or MP3 file at 320kbps/16 bit with a sample rate of 44.1kHz' (https://support.routenote.com/kb-article/what-are-the-audio-file-requirements/). Quality standards confirmed: RouteNote flags clipped/peaking audio, and 'Tracks should not have more than eight seconds of silence at the start or end'; it also lists muffled/muddy recordings, hum/buzz/hiss, room echo, heavy compression, audio that is too quiet/loud, and skipping audio as rejection risks (https://support.routenote.com/kb-article/does-my-audio-meet-routenotes-quality-standards/). Minimum lengths: release total 30 s or longer; each track 3 s or longer.
evidence_quote: $10 – Single [1 Track] ... $20 – EP [2 – 6 Tracks] ... $30 – Album [7 – 18 Tracks] ... $45 – Extended Album [19+ Tracks]. After your first year, there's a $9.99 annual subscription fee if you choose to keep the release Premium. | Audio must be formatted in stereo as a FLAC or MP3 file at 320kbps/16 bit with a sample rate of 44.1kHz. | Tracks should not have more than eight seconds of silence at the start or end.

claim: KOMCA (Korea Music Copyright Association) announced AI-assisted music registration criteria on 2026-08-03 and withdrew them on 2026-08-25 at its 8th board meeting; new AI-assisted works are on hold until new rules. Sources: https://www.khan.co.kr/article/202608251836001/ and https://sports.khan.co.kr/article/202608251932003/
correction: Accurate as of 2026-09-06. KOMCA's new 'AI-assisted musical work' filing/registration criteria (human must have substantially and leadingly participated in lyrics/composition/arrangement; 100% prompt-only AI output excluded) took effect on 2026-08-03 (press coverage dated Aug 3-4, 2026). On 2026-08-25, at its 8th board meeting (제8회 이사회), KOMCA voted to withdraw the related amendments to the '음악저작물 신고·등록에 관한 규정' and '음악저작권 신탁계약약관', citing an MCST letter (Aug 18) and National Assembly requests for broader cultural-sector consensus first. Per the coverage: works received but not yet registered are held (유보) until a new policy exists; works that were registered during the ~3-week window are subject to registration-cancellation procedures. KOMCA frames this as a temporary pause, not a denial of AI-assisted copyright. Caveat: both Khan URLs were egress-blocked in this environment; the facts were verified through search-engine summaries of those same Khan articles plus Korea JoongAng Daily, Asiae (English), MLex and keyzard.cc snippets, which all agree on the dates and board-meeting number.

claim: Korean subscription streaming revenue split under the MCST-approved rules: platform 35%, producers/master 48.25%, songwriters/publishing 10.5%, performers 6.25%. A 2025 proposal to change to 68.42/31.58 was discussed for June 2026 but its approval status is unclear.
correction: The split figures are correct; the '68.42/31.58 proposal' could not be found anywhere. Current rule: MCST approved the amended 음원 전송사용료 징수규정 of the four music CMOs (KOMCA, KOSCAP, FKMP, RIAK) on 2018-06-20, effective 2019-01-01, raising the on-demand streaming rights-holder share from 60:40 to 65:35 (download stays 70:30). Within the 65% rights-holder share: record producers/masters 48.25%, authors (composers/lyricists) 10.5%, performers 6.25%; the service provider keeps 35%. This 35/48.25/10.5/6.25 breakdown is confirmed as still the operative framework in coverage dated Dec 2025 (Asiae) and by the Korea Music Content Association's 2021 fact-check. No source in six targeted searches (Korean and English) mentions any 68.42% / 31.58% ratio, any proposal to adopt it, or a June 2026 decision on it; treat that sentence as unsupported and remove or re-source it. What does exist: on 2025-12-24 MCST opened public comment (through 2026-01-08) on a KOMCA 사용료 징수규정 amendment covering on-demand streaming unit price, a revised music-usage-fee rate, and a new short-form (숏폼) fee; its approval status as of 2026-09-06 could not be verified because mcst.go.kr and copyright.or.kr are blocked here. Caveat: all primary pages (mcst.go.kr, korea.kr, copyright.or.kr, findcopyright.or.kr) were egress-blocked; figures verified via search-engine summaries of those pages.

claim: Amuse releases: 10 per 7 days.
correction: As of 2026-09-06, the 10-per-7-days cap applies only to releases that contain AI-generated recordings, not to all releases. Amuse's Terms of Use: no more than ten (10) Releases in any rolling seven (7) day period per account where each such Release includes one or more AI-generated Recordings, unless Amuse expressly permits otherwise. The Artist plan otherwise advertises unlimited releases. Violations can lead to removal of content or account, withheld earnings, or a frozen account.
evidence_quote: [Search-index snippet of Amuse Terms of Use; direct fetch blocked] "Per Account, you will not upload more than ten (10) Releases during any rolling seven (7) day period where each such Release includes one or more Recordings generated using artificial intelligence, unless otherwise expressly permitted." Amuse Support summarises it as "a limit of 10 AI-generated releases per week."

claim: TuneCore only allows generative-AI music made with fully licensed datasets.
correction: As of 2026-09-06, TuneCore's GenAI Music Content Framework states it only distributes music created using GenAI models trained on fully licensed datasets; music from models relying on unlicensed datasets is not eligible. TuneCore will not distribute works that are 100% AI-generated. Artists are told to check the AI tool's documentation/terms for its training-data sourcing; tools that do not disclose this may not qualify. TuneCore names Google Flow Music as a partner whose output is distribution-ready.
evidence_quote: [Search-index snippet of TuneCore Support; direct fetch blocked] "TuneCore only distributes music created using GenAI models trained on fully licensed datasets." ... "Music created using models that rely on unlicensed datasets is not eligible for distribution through TuneCore." ... "TuneCore will not distribute any works that are 100% AI-generated."

claim: TuneCore requires human creation to be clear, provable and dominant.
correction: As of 2026-09-06, the substance is right (TuneCore refuses 100% AI-generated works and frames AI as enhancing, not replacing, human creation), but the exact phrase "clear, provable and dominant" could not be found on any TuneCore-owned page via search; it appears in third-party coverage (a distributor policy roundup and reports of a TuneCore CEO interview). If quoting TuneCore's official wording, use: "TuneCore will not distribute any works that are 100% AI-generated" and "AI technology is here to enhance human creativity, not replace it." Attribute the "clear, provable and dominant" wording to press/interview coverage, not to TuneCore's help center.
evidence_quote: [Third-party search-index snippet, not a TuneCore page] "TuneCore will not accept 100% AI generated music, however AI used in the creative process is allowed, so long as human creation is 'clear, provable and dominant.'" [TuneCore Support snippet] "TuneCore believes that AI technology is here to enhance human creativity, not replace it. ... TuneCore will not distribute any works that are 100% AI-generated."

claim: CD Baby rejects fully AI-generated music.
correction: As of 2026-09-06, the claim understates the policy: CD Baby rejects any AI-generated content, not just fully AI-generated tracks. Its help center says it cannot accept AI-generated content even if commercially licensed, and even when the uploader contributed original sounds and only part of the recording is AI. AI content found in an account is removed from distribution, and repeated attempts can end the relationship. The Downtown Music Content Policy (CD Baby's parent) additionally prohibits content created wholly or primarily by AI models trained on copyrighted recordings without a license, and AI content mimicking popular artists. Third-party guides state AI production tools (mastering, mixing, stem separation) on fully human-made music are acceptable, but that exception was not verifiable on a CD Baby page through my access.
evidence_quote: [Search-index snippet of CD Baby Help Center; direct fetch blocked] "CD Baby cannot accept any AI-generated content, even if it's commercially licensed. Even if you contributed original sounds to the recording, and only part of the recording is AI, we are still unable to distribute this content." ... "If CD Baby finds that you've delivered AI-generated content through your account, they will remove it from distribution, and continued attempts to distribute AI content may result in them no longer being able to work with you."

claim: LANDR limits distribution to 12 songs per month.
correction: As of 2026-09-06, LANDR's current support article states a maximum of thirty (30) AI-generated songs per calendar month per subscriber (search index dates the article to August 2026); the limit applies to AI-generated songs, not to all songs. The figure of 12 AI-generated songs per month still appears on older LANDR marketing pages for its AI tools (AI Stem Generator, AI Guitarist, AI Bassist, AI Drummer, AI Pianist) and appears outdated. Exceeding the limit may cause delays, removal of excess submissions, or upload restrictions. LANDR also reserves the right not to distribute (or to ban) music that relies entirely on AI audio generation and does not distribute AI-generated cover songs.
evidence_quote: [Search-index snippet of LANDR Support; direct fetch blocked] "LANDR accepts music created with the assistance of AI tools, but to support a fair and reliable distribution experience for all customers, artists may submit a maximum of thirty (30) AI-generated songs per calendar month per subscriber." [Older LANDR marketing pages] "Artists may submit a maximum of 12 AI-generated songs per month to LANDR Distribution."

claim: LANDR excludes AI-generated music from Content ID.
correction: As of 2026-09-06, LANDR's monetization requirements state that YouTube Content ID cannot be obtained for music that uses un-edited royalty-free loops, AI-generated music, or samples, and that music must not be fully AI-generated to qualify. Eligibility is decided at the release level: if one track fails, the whole release is ineligible for YouTube Content ID, TikTok, and Meta monetization. A Distribution or LANDR Studio subscription is required for monetization.

"Monetization is applied at the release level, not the track level ... If even one track on your release doesn't meet monetization requirements, the entire release will be ineligible."
